question_text: Does the combined void/web endpoint protocol contain enough frozen source-side and scoring-grammar material to make a go/no-go authorization decision?
reviewer_rationale: Yes. The package contains a frozen combined void/web multiblock endpoint protocol, the authorization policy/template, the FLRW consistency audit, the source-grounding gate, and the readiness-after-FLRW-audit summary. The protocol declares observable blocks, included and disabled channel families, baseline/nuisance/covariance policies, a unified AIC shell, joint null controls, pass-condition shell, forbidden inputs, and allowed outputs. The package manifest SHA-256 and byte counts were checked against the extracted files and all matched; the manifest marks every bundled artifact as containing no endpoint residuals, endpoint scores, or fit statistics.

question_text: Is it clear that the current readiness ledger has endpoint_ready_count=0 and that authorization would be permission to run one predeclared combined test, not promotion of existing pilots?
reviewer_rationale: Caveated yes. The readiness summary explicitly records endpoint_ready_count=0, support_ready_count=1, endpoint_scoring_allowed=false, and physical_validation_claimed=false. The caveat is essential: authorization here is only permission for one future, separate, predeclared combined void/web multiblock endpoint run under the frozen protocol; it is not promotion of the existing isolated pilots and not a physical-validation claim.

question_text: Can the authorization decision be made without using forbidden endpoint information or post-hoc block/channel choices?
reviewer_rationale: Yes. The authorization decision can be made from the packaged source-side governance artifacts only. I did not use distance, growth, lensing, or CMB residuals; endpoint scores; fit statistics; post-hoc block weights; post-hoc covariance reweighting; or post-hoc channel promotion. The protocol and policy explicitly prohibit those inputs, and forbidden_inputs_used remains false.

question_text: Should one separate, predeclared combined void/web multiblock endpoint run be authorized while keeping physical_validation_claimed=false?
reviewer_rationale: GO_COMBINED_VOID_WEB_ENDPOINT_PERMISSION_ONLY. I authorize only one separate, explicitly predeclared combined void/web multiblock endpoint run under the frozen protocol, with the declared unified information criterion and joint null/block-drop controls. This permission does not validate Tau Core cosmology, does not validate the void/web branch, does not score the current package, and must keep physical_validation_claimed=false.
